title: Transfer: momentum and impulse
target: Apply momentum reasoning to new collisions and deflection cases.
criteria: Define the system and positive direction.
Use conservation or impulse only when assumptions apply.
Explain energy and model limits clearly.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A ball collides with a cart. To use total momentum conservation, which choice is appropriate?
options: Analyze only the ball while ignoring the cart force.
Assign a different unconverted sign convention to each object.
Assume every individual momentum is conserved.
Include both objects, choose one axis, and check external impulse.
cpa.guide: System, common axis, and external-impulse condition are essential.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Take west as positive. A 2 kg cart moves east at 7 m/s. What is its momentum?
cpa.guide: East is negative under this convention; p = 2(−7) = −14.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 4 kg cart slows from +6 to +1 m/s over 2 s. What is average net force?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two objects have initial total momentum +22 kg·m/s and receive external impulse −6 N·s. What is final total momentum?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: An isolated collision conserves momentum but loses kinetic energy. What follows?
options: Both objects must have negative mass.
It is inelastic; energy has changed form or transferred within the full account.
cpa.guide: Kinetic energy is only one part of total energy.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A tiny impulse is predicted to produce a large offset after a long time. What should be checked before applying that prediction to an asteroid?
options: Target mass, lead time, ejecta, and orbital assumptions.
Whether all gravity can be ignored forever.
cpa.guide: The simple impulse-and-drift model requires explicit limits in a real orbital setting.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
